(There, se'if 6) Even though women are exempt, they may blow. Gloss: See the Magen Avraham, who was astonished at the Bach (for behold we hold that [regarding] a minor who eats neveilos, the court is not commanded to restrain him) see there. And in my humble opinion there is no difficulty: for there is a distinction whether the nevelah belongs to the minor or to the adult. That [ruling that] a minor who eats neveilos (the court is not commanded to restrain him) is when the nevelah is the minor's, or belongs to others who are not before us; in that case those who see him need not restrain him, for it is not like giving it into his hands. But if the nevelah belongs to the adult, and the adult sees him and does not protest against him, then it is like giving it into his hands. And so here too the case is that the shofar belongs to the adult; therefore regarding a woman and a minor one is not obligated to protest, but regarding a deaf person and a shoteh one is obligated to protest, so it appears to my humble opinion, correct and clear; and examine carefully. And behold, see the source of this se'if's law in the Gemara and the Rishonim: and from this it is clear that they ruled like R' Yosi, that women's leaning [on a korban] is optional. And behold, this is evident from the language of the Rambam in chapter 3 of Maaseh HaKorbanos, halachah 5: "Olot of gentiles; they do not bring drink-offerings with them, etc., and they do not require leaning, for leaning applies only to Yisrael, to men and not to women" (end quote). Behold, from this language "they do not require leaning," it is implied that if he wishes he may lean; and it is evident that he rules like R' Yosi that it is optional. And behold, thereby one may resolve the words of the Rambam in chapter 3 of Hilchos Chagigah, halachah 3, and this is his language: a tumtum and an androginos are exempt because they are a doubtful woman. And the Lechem Mishneh there already wondered that this contradicts the Gemara of Chagigah, folio 4, which says that this is derived from the verse "your males," and also objects there that a tumtum is a doubt (does a verse come to exclude a doubt?) and answers: when his testicles are outside; and the Rambam omitted this. He also wrote that an androginos is [exempt] because of a doubtful woman, whereas the Gemara says he is a distinct creature (see there, where he left it as requiring further study). And what appeared to me to resolve it is as follows. From the outset I found difficult against the Rambam: what of it that he is a doubtful woman; nevertheless he is obligated to fulfill the mitzvah out of doubt, as is the law of every Torah doubt; and even according to the Rambam that every Torah doubt is [treated as] rabbinic, nevertheless by rabbinic law he would be obligated to fulfill. And it is resolved for me: since it is heads-or-tails, if he brings korbanos they are chullin in the [Temple] courtyard; and if he brings and stipulates on condition that if not [he is obligated] it should be a freewill offering (freewill vows and donations are not offered on Yom Tov; and to offer after Yom Tov) since it was not fit on the first day it is not fit on the second, since we hold that all are make-ups for the first. And so heads-or-tails: if he offers there is a prohibition as above, and without a korban there is a prohibition the other way, for "and they shall not appear before Me empty" is written; therefore Shev ve'al taaseh is preferable. And afterward I saw in Tosafos on that sugya that they wrote likewise. But it is still difficult for me: for we say in Eruvin, folio 97, that Yonah's wife would go up for the pilgrimage festival and the Sages did not protest against her, and the Gemara there establishes it according to the view that women's leaning is optional; and Tosafos wrote there that according to R' Yehudah they needed to protest against her because of the korban, which would be chullin in the courtyard (see there); if so it is implied that according to R' Yosi she would also bring a korban. And so, since it is optional, all the more so we should say that one might have thought to be stringent: what should he do with the korban; even were he a woman, she too is permitted to offer, and there is no opposite concern of prohibition. But it appears that, aside from what is written in Eruvin, folio 97, where it objects: but is an anonymous Sifra not [according to] R' Yehudah, etc., and so here too this beraisa of "your males" to exclude a tumtum and an androginos is likewise Sifra and is R' Yehudah's; and R' Yehudah holds that women are forbidden to lean. Aside from this as well, it is evident that it accords with R' Yehudah: for if it were according to R' Yosi, from where would we exclude a tumtum and an androginos from "your males" more than saying it comes to exclude women, as the language implies? And if from the language "male" that too would be implied (then why [say] "your males"? Perhaps it comes to exclude women [even] from the optional [ascent], that they are forbidden to go up) and from where that it comes to exclude a tumtum and an androginos from obligation? Of necessity it accords with R' Yehudah. And so, since throughout the Torah they are forbidden to go up, "your males" is not needed to exclude [women], and of necessity it comes to exclude a tumtum, etc. And according to this it is well. For behold the Chavvos Daas wrote, and so other authors, that the Torah spoke only of a certainty; and this is an explicit Gemara in Sotah, folio 25, regarding Rabban Gamliel who posed: it is written "every pure person shall eat meat" a certain pure person shall eat, but a doubtful pure person shall not eat, etc. And so the Gemara's objection is thus: why do we need "your males" if only "male" were written we would also exclude a doubt, for "male" implies a certain male and not a doubt; and so why "your males"? And to this it objects: granted regarding an androginos there is no difficulty, for one may say that this beraisa accords with the view that he is a distinct creature and needs "your males"; but a tumtum is a doubt (and would a verse come to exclude a doubt?) in astonishment; for if only "male" were written, that too would imply "and not a doubt" from the language "male"; and even without any verse at all we would exempt him, for automatically, since a Torah doubt [is treated] stringently, there is the opposite concern: perhaps he is a woman, and one cannot offer, since it accords with R' Yehudah that women are forbidden to lean; certainly Shev ve'al taaseh is preferable. Therefore it is necessary to answer "when his testicles are outside." And behold this is according to R' Yehudah; but for us, since we hold like R' Yosi that women's leaning is optional, and behold although the Gemara brings a beraisa in Eruvin that regarding Yonah's wife the Sages did not protest against her, Tosafos brought the Pesikta that the Sages did protest against her, and according to this one may say that the Rambam rules like R' Yosi and rules according to the Pesikta that the Sages protested against her; that is, that even according to R' Yosi she is forbidden to lean, for "your males" excludes women even from the optional. And so "your males" comes to exclude women; and a tumtum and an androginos in truth need no verse, for they are a doubtful woman, and they cannot be stringent, for there is a prohibition the other way; that women are forbidden to go up. Automatically one may say that if his testicles are outside, so that it is known he is truly male, he is in fact obligated to go up. And that the Rambam did not clarify that women are forbidden to go up is because it is automatically implied: since he exempts a doubtful woman, [and] a Torah doubt [is] for stringency, of necessity it is impossible to "fix" [the matter], for there is a prohibition the other way. And what of it that she is a woman; [if] a woman is optional, of necessity he holds that a woman is forbidden to lean; and it is evident that he rules like the Pesikta. Also it is not his way to write what is not explicit in the Gemara, as is known of his way. So it appears to my humble opinion, correct, with the help of Hashem; and examine carefully.
(There, se'if 6 in the gloss) And the custom is that women recite the blessing over time-bound positive mitzvos; therefore here too they should recite the blessing for themselves, etc. Gloss: Behold I saw in Sefer Shemos BaAretz on Rosh Hashanah, folio 33, that he raised a difficulty that the Tur's words contradict one another: for here he wrote that they may recite the blessing if they wish, and above in siman 17 regarding tzitzis he wrote that it is better that they not recite the blessing (see there, where he was pressed in his resolution). And in my humble opinion one may say thus: for if women do not intend to "add," there is no prohibition that they recite the blessing, for to transgress "do not add" requires intent; and if they do not intend to add, there is no prohibition in their blessing, only that we hold that in its proper time one transgresses "do not add" without intent; therefore it is proper that they not recite the blessing, for then there is a distinguishing sign that they are not doing it for the sake of the mitzvah, as he wrote something similar in the name of the Mordechai: that therefore there is no concern of "do not add," since they do not recite the blessing; brought in the Shulchan Aruch of the Gaon, the pious Moreinu HaRav R' Eliyahu of Vilna, of blessed memory, siman 667. But one may say: regarding women today is not "its time," and so relative to them it is counted as not in its time, and then intent is required; and since they do not intend to add, why should they not recite the blessing? But one may say that this depends on whether women are counted as a people of their own or not; and see regarding this a dispute in tractate Shabbos, chapter 6, folio 62 (see there). And if we say women are a people of their own, relative to them it is counted as not in its time and intent is required; but if we say they are not a people of their own, then since it is its time for males, regarding women too one transgresses "do not add" without intent. And according to this one may say thus: regarding a time-bound positive mitzvah from which males are obligated and it is impossible to exempt oneself from it at all (and since women are exempt and men are truly obligated) women are counted as a people of their own, and for them it is not its time, and intent is required. But regarding a time-bound positive mitzvah from which males too have a side by which to exempt themselves, in that case women are not counted as a people of their own. Similar to what we say in Menachos regarding same-species [mixing]: that where it is possible to be like its fellow it is counted as same-species (see there); so one may say here. And therefore regarding shofar, where males are obligated and it is impossible to exempt oneself from it, and it is truly a personal obligation, therefore women are counted as a people of their own, and it is not its time, and "do not add" does not apply; therefore they are permitted to recite the blessing. But regarding tzitzis, which is an obligation of the garment and not a personal obligation, in that case, since even upon males there is no absolute obligation, and it is in his hand to exempt himself if he does not wear a four-cornered garment, therefore they are not counted as a people of their own, and it is counted as its time for women too, since it is its time for men; therefore intent is not required to transgress; therefore the Tur wrote that it is better that she not recite the blessing. So it appears to my humble opinion, correct in reason and as a practical ruling in this. And see what I wrote as a proof for the Tur in my novellae on Orach Chaim from the year 596, in siman 627 (see there); and examine. And see what I wrote as a proof for this ruling of the Rama here in my composition on Orach Chaim from the year 604, in a responsum to the holy community of Krakow, in Hilchos Sukkah, siman 631 (see there); and examine. And see the Magen Avraham here, s.k. 5, what he wrote in the name of the Radbaz regarding one who comes to the synagogue, etc. and see regarding this in my composition on Hilchos Niddah, siman 598, in a responsum to the land of Hungary, there at length, what I wrote to raise a difficulty against him from the Gemara (see there); and examine.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ו] [לבוש] קודם שיתקעו בבית הכנסת וכו'. אבל במעגלי צדק כתב בשם מהרי"ל שלא יתקע בשלוש ראשונות משום דמיפקד דינא כמו שכתב סוף סימן תקצ"א, לכן יתקע להם אחר תקיעת בית הכנסת, עד כאן, ואם כן לא יוכל לברך להם. ולכן נראה לי דאם יש לו שופר אחר יתקע בשעת תקיעת בית הכנסת דאז אפילו הוא תוך שלוש ראשונות אין לחוש ואם לאו יכוין בלבו שלא לצאת בתקיעת בית הכנסת ואז יוכל לברך להם, מגן אברהם. ולעניות דעתי אפשר גם דעת מעגלי צדק כן שכתב זה לשונו, יתקעו מיד אחר שיתקעו בבית הכנסת עד כאן לשונו, ושינה מלשון מהרי"ל שכתב אחר שיתקעו אלא דמיד אחר שיודעין שהתחילו קאמר ועיין סימן תקפ"ה:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [6] [Levush] Before they blow in the synagogue, etc. But in Maaglei Tzedek he wrote in the name of the Maharil that one should not blow during the first three [hours], because judgment is then appointed, as he wrote at the end of siman 591; therefore he should blow for them after the synagogue tekiah (end quote). And if so, he cannot recite the blessing for them. Therefore it appears to me that if he has another shofar he should blow at the time of the synagogue tekiah, for then even if it is within the first three there is no concern; and if not, he should intend in his heart not to fulfill his obligation with the synagogue tekiah, and then he can recite the blessing for them. Magen Avraham. And in my humble opinion it is also possible that Maaglei Tzedek's view is thus, for he wrote this wording: "they should blow immediately after they blow in the synagogue" end of his wording; and he changed from the Maharil's wording who wrote "after they blow," but rather he means immediately after they know that they have begun (and see siman 585).

magen_avraham.he:
יכולות לתקוע. ולא אמרי' דיש בו משום שבות וה"ה קטן אין מוחין בידו אבל לחרש ושוט' מוחין לתקוע שאינן באין לידי חיוב בשום פנים (ב"ח) ודבריו צ"ע דהא אין ב"ד מצווין להפרישו אפי' אוכל נבילות כדאית' ביבמות פי"ד ע"ש ועסי' רס"ו ס"ה ועסי' שמ"ג ולכן נ"ל דנקט קטנים ונשים לרבותא דאע"ג דבני דעת נינהו רשאין לתקוע עסי' תקצ"ו:
כבר יצאו כו'. לכן יתקע להם קוד' שישמע התקיעות בבה"כ (לבוש) אבל במ"צ כתב בשם מהרי"ל שלא יתקע בג' ראשונות משום דמיפקד דינא כמ"ש סי' תקצ"א, לכן יתקע להם אחר תקיעת בה"כ עכ"ל לא יוכל לברך להם לכן נ"ל דאם יש לו שופר אחר יתקע בשעת תקיע' בה"כ דאז אפי' הוא תוך ג' ראשונו' אין לחוש כמ"ש שם ואם לאו יכוין בלבו שלא לצאת בתקיעת בה"כ ואז יוכל לברך להם עססי' ו' אך בזה יש לדקדק אם הליכה מביתו לבה"כ חשיב הפסק ויצטרך לברך שנית על התקיעות ששומע בבה"כ על סדר הברכות כמ"ש סי' ח' סי"ג ומ"מ נ"ל דא"צ לברך כמ"ש סי' תקצ"ב ס"ג ול"ד לציצית שב' מצות הן משא"כ הכא דכולה חדא מצוה כמ"ש הרי"ף סוף ר"ה ע"ש, מי שבא לבה"כ לצאת י"ח עם הצבור אע"פי שבשעה ששמע לא כוון לבו אלא סתמא יצא אבל הבא לבה"כ בסתמא לא יצא (רדב"ז ח"א ק"ס):
magen_avraham.en:
They may blow. And we do not say that there is in it a [concern of] shevus; and likewise a minor; we do not protest against him. But for a deaf person and a shoteh we protest against blowing, for they never come to obligation in any way (Bach). And his words require further study, for behold the court is not commanded to restrain him even if he eats neveilos, as is found in Yevamos, chapter 14 (see there); and see siman 266, se'if 5; and see siman 343. Therefore it appears to me that he mentioned minors and women for an additional point: that even though they are people of understanding, they are permitted to blow (see siman 596).
They have already fulfilled, etc. Therefore he should blow for them before he hears the tekios in the synagogue (Levush). But in Maaglei Tzedek he wrote in the name of the Maharil that one should not blow during the first three [hours], because judgment is then appointed, as is written in siman 591; therefore he should blow for them after the synagogue tekiah (end quote). He will not be able to recite the blessing for them; therefore it appears to me that if he has another shofar he should blow at the time of the synagogue tekiah, for then even if it is within the first three there is no concern, as is written there; and if not, he should intend in his heart not to fulfill his obligation with the synagogue tekiah, and then he can recite the blessing for them (see se'if 6). But in this one must carefully consider whether walking from his house to the synagogue is considered an interruption, so that he would need to recite the blessing a second time over the tekios he hears in the synagogue in the order of the blessings, as is written in siman 8, se'if 13. Nevertheless it appears to me that he need not recite the blessing, as is written in siman 592, se'if 3; and it is unlike tzitzis, which are two mitzvos (which is not so here, for it is all one mitzvah, as the Rif wrote at the end of Rosh Hashanah) see there. One who comes to the synagogue to fulfill his obligation with the congregation (even though at the time he heard he did not direct his heart, but only in a general way) has fulfilled; but one who comes to the synagogue in a general way has not fulfilled (Radbaz, part 1, [siman] 160).

mishnah_berurah.he:
(ח) יכולות לתקוע - ולא אמרינן דכיון דפטורות יש חילול יו"ט בתקיעתן דקי"ל גדול המצווה ועושה ממי שאינו מצווה ועושה אלמא דמי שאינו מצווה ועושה נמי שכר יש לו. וה"ה קטן יכול לתקוע אף לכתחלה כדי שיתחנך וכדאיתא לקמן בסימן תקצ"ו בהג"ה:
(ט) וכן אחר שיצא כבר - ר"ל אף שיצא ולא אמרינן דכיון שהוא עצמו אינו צריך עתה לתקוע תו עובר משום שבות כשתוקע בשבילן דמ"מ קצת מצוה יש להן בתקיעתן כנ"ל:
(י) אבל אין מברכות וכו' - דמהו וציונו בדבר שאינה מחוייבת לא מד"ת ולא מדברי סופרים דאשה במ"ע שהזמן גרמא פטורות אף מדרבנן:
(יא) אם כבר יצאו - וע"כ י"א דיתקע להם קודם שישמע התקיעות בביהכ"נ אבל במ"א מסיק בשם מהרי"ל שלא יתקע בשלשה שעות ראשונות משום דאז מיפקד דינא ואין כדאי לתקוע ביחידות אלא יתקע להן אחר תקיעות ביהכ"נ והם יברכו לעצמן או שיכוין בלבו שלא לצאת בתקיעות ביהכ"נ ואז יוכל אח"כ ג"כ לברך בשבילן:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(8) They may blow, and we do not say that since they are exempt there is a desecration of Yom Tov in their blowing; for we hold "greater is one who is commanded and does than one who is not commanded and does" hence one who is not commanded and does also has reward. And likewise a minor may blow even l'chatchila in order to train him, as is found below in siman 596 in the gloss.
(9) And likewise another who has already fulfilled, that is to say, even if he has already fulfilled; and we do not say that since he himself does not now need to blow, he then transgresses a shevus when he blows for them, for nevertheless they have some mitzvah in their blowing, as above.
(10) But they do not recite the blessing, etc., for what "and commanded us" is there regarding a matter in which she is not obligated, neither by Torah law nor by the words of the Scribes; for a woman regarding time-bound positive mitzvos is exempt even by rabbinic law.
(11) If they have already fulfilled, and therefore there are those who say he should blow for them before he hears the tekios in the synagogue. But the Magen Avraham concludes in the name of the Maharil that one should not blow during the first three hours, because then judgment is appointed, and it is not worthwhile to blow as an individual; rather he should blow for them after the synagogue tekios, and they should recite the blessing for themselves, or he should intend in his heart not to fulfill his obligation with the synagogue tekios, and then afterward he can also recite the blessing on their behalf.

kaf_hachayyim.he: ו) [סעיף ב'] חרש שוטה וקטן פטורין. סומא חייב בכל מצות התורה ובתקיעה מה"ת ומוציא את אחרים י"ח. ורי"ו בנתיב י"ג ח"א חולק וכתב הרדב"ז בח"א סי' נ"ט דאין לחוש לסברתו. כנה"ג בהגה"ט וכ"כ הפר"ח בסעי' ד' דסומא חייב מה"ת ומוציא אחרים י"ח ואין לחוש לסברת רי"ו שכתב דלא מחייב אלא מדרבנן יעו"ש. ועיין באו' שאח"ז.
kaf_hachayyim.en: 6) [Seif 2] A deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person, and minor are exempt. A blind person is obligated in all the commandments of the Torah and in shofar by Torah law, and may discharge the obligation of others. Rabbeinu Yeruham, Netiv 13, part 1, disagrees. Radbaz, part 1, siman 59, writes that one need not take his view into account. Knesset HaGedolah, Hagahot Tur. So too Peri Chadash, seif 4, writes that a blind person is obligated by Torah law and may discharge the obligation of others, and that one need not take account of Rabbeinu Yeruham's view that his obligation is only rabbinic; see there. See the following letter:

mechaber.he: המודר הנאה מחבירו מותר לתקוע לו תקיעה של מצוה ודוקא שהוא תוקע מאליו להוציאו אבל אם אמר לו המודר תקע והוציאני אסור: הגה ואם אמר קונם תקיעותיו עלי בכל ענין אסור: (ר"ן):
mechaber.en: If somebody swears off benefiting from his friend, that friend is permitted to sound a shofar for him to fulfill the obligation. This is only the case when he sounds the shofar unprompted to fulfill his obligation. But if the swearer says "Blow to fulfill my obligation," this is forbidden. {Rama: Rema: If he says "His soundings are konam to me," it is always forbidden (Ra"n).}

beer_hagolah.en:
(א) M.M. Darb is there

(ב) The mountain

beur_hagra.he:
ס"ז ודוקא כו'. ע' תוס' דנדרים ל"ה ב' ד"ה איבעיא להו כו':
אבל אם אמר. שם ל"ה ב' כנ"ל ול"ו ב':
ואם אמרי' כנ"ל בסי' תקס"ו:
beur_hagra.en:
Se'if 7. And specifically, etc. See Tosafos of Nedarim 35b, s.v. "A question was raised before them," etc.
But if he said. There, 35b, as above; and 36b.
And if we say as above in siman 566.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ז] קונם תקיעתו וכו'. נתבאר בסימן תקפ"ה סעיף ה':
eliyah_rabbah.en: [7] "Konam" his blowing, etc. It is explained in siman 585, se'if 5.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(יב) המודר הנאה וכו' - כגון ראובן שהדיר ע"ע שלא יהנה משמעון אפ"ה מותר לשמעון לתקוע לו דמצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו ואין תקיעות מצוה בכלל איסור הנאה שאסר ע"ע משא"כ כשאסר תקיעותיו אסר אפילו בזה שאינו הנאה:
(יג) מאליו - אפי' כשאומר מי שרוצה להוציאני ידי חובתי יתקע שרי דבכה"ג לאו שליחותיה קעביד:
(יד) והוציאני אסור - דכיון דבשליחותיה עביד יש לו הנאה במאי דעביד שליחותיה ובדיעבד יצא [פמ"ג בשם הפר"ח]:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(12) One who vowed not to benefit, etc., for example, Reuven who vowed upon himself not to benefit from Shimon: even so, Shimon is permitted to blow for him, for mitzvos were not given for the sake of benefit, and mitzvah tekios are not included in the benefit-prohibition he imposed upon himself, which is not so when he forbade [Shimon's] tekios themselves: he forbade even this, which is not benefit.
(13) Of his own accord; even when he says, "Whoever wishes to discharge me of my obligation should blow," it is permitted; for in such a case he is not performing his agency.
(14) "And discharge me" is forbidden, for since he acts as his agent, he has benefit in that his agency is performed; and after the fact he has fulfilled [Peri Megadim in the name of the Peri Chadash].

kaf_hachayyim.he: ז) היה מחזיק במצות התקיעה וסלקוהו מפני סברת רי"ו אם לא ימצאו תוקע בקי כמוהו יחזירוהו למינויו ואם ימצאו מי שהוא בקי כמוהו יעמוד השני בחזקתו וראשון כיון שנדחה נדחה כיון שיצא מפי רי"ו הרדב"ז שם. כנה"ג שם. מ"א סק"ב. וכבר כתבנו עוד מזה לעיל סי' ג"ן או' ס"ה קחנו משם:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 7) If he had an established right to the mitzvah of sounding the shofar and they removed him because of Rabbeinu Yerucham's view, then if they cannot find a proficient shofar blower equal to him, they should restore him to his appointment. If they find someone equally proficient, the second person retains his established position, and the first, once displaced, remains displaced, since the view was issued by Rabbeinu Yerucham. Radbaz, ibid.; Knesset HaGedolah, ibid.; Magen Avraham, s.k. 2. We have already written further concerning this above, siman 53, os 65; take it from there.

mechaber.he: המתעסק בתקיעת שופר להתלמד לא יצא ידי חובתו וכן השומע מן המתעסק לא יצא וכן התוקע לשורר ולא נתכוון לתקיעת מצוה לא יצא נתכוין שומע לצאת ידי חובתו ולא נתכוון התוקע להוציאו או שנתכוון התוקע להוציאו ולא נתכוון השומע לצאת לא יצא ידי חובתו עד שיתכוון שומע ומשמיע:
mechaber.en: Someone who is engaged in blowing a shofar in order to practice doesn't fulfil his obligation. Similarly, someone who hears shofar from someone such a person doesn't fulfil his obligation. Similarly, someone who is blowing the shofar to make music and doesn't intend for the mitzva of blowing the shofar doesn't fulfil his obligation. If the listener intends to fulfil the mitzva but the blower doesn't have intent for him or if blower has intent for him but the listener does not; he doesn't fulfil his obligation until the two of them have intent, the listener and the blower.

chokhmat_shlomo.he: (שם סעיף ח) המתעסק בתקיעת שופר להתלמד לא יצא ידי חובתו וכו' נ"ב הנה הר"ן כתב בסוף ר"ה במשנה דהשומע מן המתעסק לא יצא דאף למ"ד מצות א"צ כוונה הכא גרע כיון דמכוין להנך התינוקות הוי בת מינה ומחריב בה ע"ש וקשה לי טובא מן הש"ס שם דפריך השומע מן המתעסק לא יצא הא מן המשמיע לעצמו יצא לימא תיהוי תיובתא דר"ז דאמר לשמעיה אכוון ותקע לי ומשני איידי וקשה לי מה פריך לפי דעת הר"ן הנ"ל הרי י"ל דאדרבא רבותא קמ"ל דלעולם מצות א"צ כוונה ואם שמע מהתוקע שלא לשם מצוה כלל ודאי יצא ולא בעי שיכוין הלה להוציאו רק ר"ז מיירי דשמעיה כוון להוציא לעצמו לכך כיון דבת מינה הוא מחריב בה לכך צריך לכווין גם להוציא את ר"ז ולכך המשנה רבותא קמ"ל דלא מן המשמיע לעצמו דהוי לשם מצוה ממש פשיטא דנחשב בת מינה ממש ומחריב בה ולא יצא רק גם אם הוי כמתעסק אז הוי ס"ד כיון דאינו רק לחנך והשומע מכוון לשם מצוה ממש לא נקרא זה בת מינה ולא מחריב בה לכך קמ"ל דגם זה הוה בת מינה ומחריב בה ובעי כוונה וזו קושיא גדולה לדעת הר"ן לפעד"נ וצ"ע ודו"ק. גם קשה לי מאי פריך הרי י"ל כמו דקיי"ל בתופס לבע"ח במקום שחב לאחרים ל"ק ומגביה מציאה לחבירו קנה מכח מיגו דזכה לנפשיה וכו' נימא נמי בזה היכא דלא יצא עדיין התוקע לא בעי כוונה להוציא השומע מכח מגו דזכה לנפשיה אבל אם כבר יצא התוקע אז בעינן כוונה ור"ז מיירי שכבר יצא התוקע אף שדוחק לו' כן דשמעיה יהיה יוצא קודם ר"ז עכ"פ נימא דר"ז ס"ל דלכתחלה בעי בכל ענין כוונה והמשנה מיירי בדיעבד וצ"ע וד"ק: והנה מה דמבואר בש"ע המתעסק בתקיעת שופר להתלמד לא יצא ידי חובתו. הנה לכאורה אין הלשון של הש"ע מדוקדק שנקט כאן שלא כסדר עפמ"ש הר"ן במס' ר"ה בב' מקומות דאף למ"ד תקע לשיר יצא דמצות אין צריכות כוונה מודה דמתעסק לא יצא דזה גרע במה שמכוין לשם מצוה לחנך התינוקות כמ"ש במס' זבחים דבת מינה מחריב בה דלאו בת מינה לא מחריב בה ע"ש ולפ"ז אתי שפיר הש"ע תחלה כ' דתוקע כדי להתלמד לא מהני ואח"כ כתב בתוקע לשיר דלא יצא זהו דרך לא זו אף זו דל"מ כוון להתלמד דהוי בת מינה דלא יצא רק אף בתוקע לשיר דלאו בת מינה לא יצא. אך מ"ש אח"כ בנתכוין שומע ולא נתכוין משמיע להוציא השומע דלא יצא זה הוי זו ואצ"ל זו דמה אם כוון רק לחנך התינוקות דהוי בת מינה ומחריב בה מכ"ש אם כוון לצאת ממש י"ח לשם מצוה דהוי בת מינה ומחריב בה כיון דלא כיוון להוציא השומע והוי ק"ו דלא יצא דמה המתעסק לא יצא כ"ש בזה וכן הוי ק"ו מתוקע לשיר מה תוקע לשיר דלא הוי בת מינה ומחריב בה מכ"ש בתוקע לשם מצוה ואין מכוין להוציא השומע דלא יצא והוי זו ואצ"ל זו. אך הן אמת דקשה לי על הר"ן מן הש"ס דר"ה דף ל"ג דפריך שם בשומע מן המתעסק דלא יצא הא שומע מן השומע לעצמו יצא והא תניא וכו'. וקשה לפי דברי הר"ן מה פריך נימא דאדרבא רבותא קמ"ל דאף שומע מן המתעסק דלא כוון למצוה גמורה רק לחנך התינוקות והוי רק דרבנן מ"מ נקרא בת מינה ומהני דלא יצא מן התורה אף דמן התורה ליכא מצוה כלל ולא הוי מינו מן התורה מ"מ לא יצא מן התורה וחייב לחזור ולתקוע מן התורה ונ"מ לכמה דברים בין אם חייב מן התורה בין אם חייב מדרבנן מכ"ש בנתכוין לצאת מעצמו ולא כוון להוציא השומע דבזה הוי מינו ממש והוי מצוה מן התורה דהוי בת מינה ומחריב בה ובעינן כוונה לכ"ע ואם לא כוון להוציא השומע לא מהני והוי זו ואצ"ל זו ומה פריך. והנה בזה הוי א"ש לשון הש"ע דמן הש"ס הנ"ל הוכיח דהמתעסק גרע מנתכוין לעצמו ולכך כתב שפיר דרך לא זו אף זו אך אעפ"כ על הר"ן קשה שפיר דמנ"ל על הש"ס להקשות דהרי יש סברא לו' דנתכוין לעצמו גרע ממתעסק לפי סברת הר"ן הנ"ל ומה פריך וצ"ע. והנה עיינתי בלשון רש"י שכתב בד"ה מתעסק הוא דלא וכו' אבל תוקע לשיר שמתכוין לתקיעה בעלמא יצא עכ"ל. והוא תמוה דהרי הש"ס רוצה להוכיח רק דאם תוקע לשם מצוה רק שאינו מכוין להוציא השומע יצא וע"ז פריך מר"ז ול"ל להזכיר כאן תוקע לשיר. וא"ל דרש"י מפרש דמ"ש בש"ס אבל השומע מן המשמיע לעצמו היינו בתוקע לשיר שמשמיע לעצמו כלו' לדעתו ולא מכח חובת היום שמוטל עליו רק לדעתו זה אינו דרש"י כתב אח"כ בד"ה תנא סיפא נמי מתעסק וז"ל ולעולם השומע מן המשמיע לעצמו שלא נתכוין להוציא את השומעין לא יצא עכ"ל אם כן משמע שגם הוא מפרש המשמיע לעצמו הוי רק שלא כוון להוציא את השומעין אבל לעצמו כוון לצאת וכמו שמוכח מלשון ר"ז ולמה תחלה פירש כוונה לשיר וע"ק דלפי דרכו דמוכח מכאן דלשיר נמי יצא הוי ליה להקשות מזה למ"ד מצות צריכות כוונה ולמה פריך לר"ז דוקא רק הול"ל ש"מ מצות א"צ כוונה כמ"ש בברכות ובכמה דוכתי ש"מ מצות צריכות כוונה הול"ל כאן להיפוך ש"מ מצות א"צ כוונה ולמה מזכיר דברי ר"ז ובע"כ מוכח כפירוש הר"ן דתוקע לשיר גרע ממתעסק לכן פריך רק לר"ז וצ"ע ודו"ק:
chokhmat_shlomo.en: (There, se'if 8) One who is occupied with shofar-blowing in order to practice has not fulfilled his obligation, etc. Gloss: Behold the Ran wrote at the end of Rosh Hashanah on the Mishnah that one who hears from one who is so occupied has not fulfilled, for even according to the view that mitzvos do not require intent, here it is worse, since he intends for those children it is "of its kind" and ruins it (see there). And it is very difficult for me from the Gemara there, which objects: "one who hears from one who is so occupied has not fulfilled" [implying] that from one who sounds for himself he has fulfilled; let this be a refutation of R' Zeira, who said to his attendant, "Intend and blow for me" and it answers "since [the earlier clause].." And it is difficult for me: what does it object according to the Ran's view above? For one may say that on the contrary it teaches us an additional novelty: that in truth mitzvos never require intent, and if he heard from a blower not for the sake of the mitzvah at all he has certainly fulfilled, and he need not intend that the other discharge him; only that R' Zeira's case is where his attendant intended to discharge himself; therefore, since it is "of its kind," it ruins it, and therefore he must intend also to discharge R' Zeira. And therefore the Mishnah teaches us an additional novelty: not [only] from one who sounds for himself, which is truly for the sake of the mitzvah (where it is obvious that it is truly "of its kind" and ruins it, and he has not fulfilled) but even if it is like one occupied [without mitzvah intent], one might have thought that since it is only for training and the hearer intends for the sake of the mitzvah proper, this is not called "of its kind" and does not ruin it; therefore it teaches us that this too is "of its kind" and ruins it and requires intent. And this is a great difficulty against the Ran's view, in my humble opinion, and it requires further study; and examine carefully. Also it is difficult for me: what does it object, for one may say as we hold regarding one who seizes for a creditor in a place where he damages others, that he has not acquired, whereas one who lifts a find for his fellow has acquired by virtue of "since he acquired for himself," etc. say likewise here: where the blower has not yet fulfilled, he need not intend to discharge the hearer, by virtue of "since he acquired for himself"; but if the blower has already fulfilled, then we require intent; and R' Zeira's case is where the blower had already fulfilled. Even though it is forced to say that his attendant would fulfill before R' Zeira; nevertheless say that R' Zeira holds that l'chatchila intent is required in every case, and the Mishnah refers after the fact; and this requires further study; and examine carefully. And behold, that which is explained in the Shulchan Aruch ("one who is occupied with shofar-blowing in order to practice has not fulfilled his obligation") seemingly the language of the Shulchan Aruch is not precise, for he took this out of order according to what the Ran wrote in tractate Rosh Hashanah in two places: that even according to the view that one who blew for a song has fulfilled, for mitzvos do not require intent; he concedes that one who is so occupied [for practice] has not fulfilled, for this is worse in that he intends for the sake of a mitzvah of training children, as is written in tractate Zevachim that "of its kind" ruins it, whereas what is not of its kind does not ruin it (see there). And according to this the Shulchan Aruch fits well: first he wrote that blowing in order to practice does not help, and afterward he wrote regarding one who blows for a song that he has not fulfilled; this is the manner of "not only this but even that": not only where he intended to practice, which is "of its kind," has he not fulfilled, but even one who blows for a song, which is not "of its kind," has not fulfilled. But that which he wrote afterward (where the hearer intended and the sounder did not intend to discharge the hearer, that he has not fulfilled) this is "this, and it goes without saying that": for if intending only to train the children, which is "of its kind" and ruins it, all the more so if he intended actually to fulfill his own obligation for the sake of the mitzvah, which is "of its kind" and ruins it, since he did not intend to discharge the hearer; and it is a fortiori that he has not fulfilled: just as the one occupied [for practice] has not fulfilled, all the more so in this case. And likewise it is a fortiori from one who blows for a song: just as one who blows for a song, which is not "of its kind," [still] ruins it, all the more so one who blows for the sake of the mitzvah and does not intend to discharge the hearer has not fulfilled; and this is "this, and it goes without saying that." But in truth it is difficult for me against the Ran from the Gemara of Rosh Hashanah, folio 33, which objects there regarding one who hears from one occupied [for practice] that he has not fulfilled (implying that one who hears from one who sounds for himself has fulfilled) and a beraisa teaches, etc. And according to the Ran's words it is difficult: what does it object? Say that on the contrary it teaches us an additional novelty: that even one who hears from one occupied [for practice], who did not intend for a complete mitzvah but only to train children, and it is only rabbinic; nevertheless it is called "of its kind" and is effective that he has not fulfilled according to the Torah, even though according to the Torah there is no mitzvah at all and it is not "its kind" according to the Torah; nevertheless he has not fulfilled according to the Torah and is obligated to blow again according to the Torah; and there is a practical difference for several matters between whether he is obligated according to the Torah or only by rabbinic law, all the more so where he intended to fulfill for himself and did not intend to discharge the hearer, for in that case it is truly "its kind" and is a Torah mitzvah, which is "of its kind" and ruins it, and all agree that intent is required, and if he did not intend to discharge the hearer it does not help; and this is "this, and it goes without saying that" so what does it object? And behold, thereby the language of the Shulchan Aruch would be well: for from that Gemara he proved that one occupied [for practice] is worse than one who intended for himself; and therefore he properly wrote in the manner of "not only this but even that." But even so, against the Ran it remains difficult: from where for the Gemara to raise a difficulty, for there is reason to say that intending for oneself is worse than being occupied [for practice], according to the Ran's reasoning above; so what does it object? And this requires further study. And behold I examined Rashi's language, who wrote s.v. "One occupied (that is not [sufficient], etc.": "but one who blows for a song, who intends for blowing in general, has fulfilled") end quote. And this is puzzling: for the Gemara wishes to prove only that if he blows for the sake of the mitzvah but does not intend to discharge the hearer, he has fulfilled; and against this it objects from R' Zeira, so why mention here one who blows for a song? And one cannot say that Rashi explains that what the Gemara wrote "but one who hears from one who sounds for himself" means one who blows for a song who sounds for himself (that is, of his own mind, and not because of the day's obligation that rests upon him, but of his own mind) for this is not so: afterward Rashi wrote s.v. "The Tanna of the latter clause also [spoke of] one occupied," and this is his language: "and in truth, one who hears from one who sounds for himself, who did not intend to discharge the hearers, has not fulfilled" (end quote). If so, it is implied that he too explains "one who sounds for himself" as merely that he did not intend to discharge the hearers, but for himself he intended to fulfill, as is evident from R' Zeira's language. So why at first did he explain an intent for a song? And it is further difficult: according to his way, that from here it is evident that for a song too he has fulfilled (he should have raised a difficulty from this against the view that mitzvos require intent; why does it object specifically against R' Zeira) rather it should have said "derive from here that mitzvos do not require intent," as is written in Berachos and in several places "derive from here that mitzvos require intent" here it should have said the opposite: "derive from here that mitzvos do not require intent." And why mention R' Zeira's words? Of necessity it is evident according to the Ran's explanation that one who blows for a song is worse than one occupied [for practice]; therefore it objects only against R' Zeira. And this requires further study; and examine carefully.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ח] להתלמד וכו'. ומכל מקום אם גם כיון לבו למצוה יצא, וכן הוא בתוספת ראש השנה:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [8] To practice, etc. Nevertheless, if he also directed his heart to the mitzvah, he has fulfilled; and so it is in Tosafos of Rosh Hashanah.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(טו) להתלמד וכו' - ואם מתכוין בזה גם לצאת ידי מצוה כתב הא"ר דיצא והיינו בעשה התקיעות כדין:
(טז) ולא נתכוון השומע לצאת - זה מיירי כשבא לביהכ"נ בסתמא אבל אם בא לביהכ"נ לצאת ידי חובה עם הצבור אע"פ שבשעה ששמע לא כיון לבו אלא בסתמא יצא:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(15) To practice, etc. (and if in this he also intends to fulfill the mitzvah, the Eliyah Rabbah wrote that he has fulfilled) that is, where he performed the tekios according to law.
(16) And the hearer did not intend to fulfill; this refers to where he came to the synagogue in a general way; but if he came to the synagogue to fulfill his obligation with the congregation, even though at the time he heard he did not direct his heart but only in a general way, he has fulfilled.

turei_zahav.he: המתעסק בתקיעו' שופר כו'. דקי"ל כמ"ד מצות צריכות כוונה כי מסיק ב"י:

kaf_hachayyim.he: ח) שם. חרש שוטה וקטן פטורין. קטן שאינו מוציא את הגדול י"ח אעפ"י שנעשה בן י"ג שנים שלמות אינו מוציא עד שידעו בו שהביא ב' שערות אחר י"ג שבדבר חיוב תורה אין סומכין על חזקה כיון שהגיע לכלל שנים הביא סימנים ואפי' למי שכמותו שכבר הוא בן י"ג וספק אם הביא ב' שערות אינו מוציא. ויש להחמיר בזה אף ביו"ט שני של ר"ה אם אפשר באחר. וכ"ז לענין להוציא את היחיד אבל לענין שיהא תוקע לצבור להוציאם י"ח יש לחזור אחר תוקע שהוא בן שלשים שנה ושאר מדות שכתבנו בסי' תקפ"א לענין תפלה ועכ"פ צריך שיתמלא זקנו כדין שליח צבור המבואר בסי' נ"ג. מט"א אד' ז' ועיין לעיל סי' נ"ה סעי' ט' וסעי' ה' וסי' נ"ג סעי' ח' ובדברינו לשם בס"ד. ועוד עיין לעיל סי' רע"א או' ט' ובחו"מ סי' ל"ה סעי' א' ובסה"ק קול יעקב סי' ט"ל או' ב' ואו' ג' ודוק:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 8) Ibid. A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor are exempt. A minor who cannot discharge an adult's obligation does not discharge it even after becoming a full 13 years old, until it is known that he developed two pubic hairs after age 13. For an obligation according to the Torah, we do not rely on the presumption that once he has reached the requisite age he has developed the signs of maturity. He cannot discharge even the obligation of one like himself, who is already 13 but whose development of two pubic hairs is uncertain. One should be stringent in this even on the second day of Rosh Hashanah, where another person is available. All this concerns discharging the obligation of an individual. However, for appointment as the shofar blower for the congregation, to discharge their obligation, one should seek a shofar blower who is 30 years old and possesses the other qualities that we wrote in siman 581 regarding prayer. At the very least, his beard must have filled out, in accordance with the law of a shaliach tzibbur explained in siman 53. Mateh Ephraim, os 7. See above, siman 55, seif 9 and seif 5, and siman 53, seif 8, and our words there, with God's help. Also see above, siman 271, os 9, and Choshen Mishpat, siman 35, seif 1, and our sefer Kaf HaChaim, Yoreh De'ah, siman 39, os 2 and os 3, and examine carefully.

mechaber.he: מי שתקע ונתכוין להוציא כל השומע תקיעתו ושמע השומע ונתכוין לצאת ידי חובתו אע"פ שאין התוקע מתכוין לפלוני זה ששמע תקיעתו ואינו יודעו יצא שהרי נתכוין להוציא לכל מי שישמענו לפיכך מי שהיה מהלך בדרך או יושב בתוך ביתו ושמע תקיעו' משליח צבור יצא אם נתכוין לצאת שהרי ש"ץ מתכוין להוציא את הרבים ידי חובתן:
mechaber.en: If somebody blows the shofar with the intention of fulfilling the obligation of every listener, and somebody hears it and has the intention to fulfill their obligation, even if the blower is not intending for this specific person who hears his blasts and doesn't know them, they fulfill their obligation, given that he had the intention to fulfill the obligation of everybody who heard him. Therefore, if somebody was walking on the street or sitting at home and heard the communal blasts, they fulfill their obligation if they have the intention to fulfill their obligation because the communal blower has the intention to fulfill the members of the community's obligations.

baer_heitev.he: בדרך. ירושלמי ל"ש אלא בעובר אבל בעומד חזקה כוון. וצ"ע הלא הוא יודע אם כוון אם לאו ואפשר דמיירי אם שכח אם כוון אם לא מ"א. מי שבא לבה"כ לצאת י"ח עם הצבור אעפ"י שבשעה ששמע לא כוון לבו אלא סתמא יצא אבל הבא לבה"כ בסתמא לא יצא הרדב"ז חלק א' סימן ק"ס. סומא חייב בתקיעה ואם היה מוחזק לתקוע בכל שנה וסלקוהו אם לא ימצא בקי כמוהו יחזירוהו למנויו. ולכתחילה אין לסלקו מפני שהוא סומא אעפ"י שנמצא בקי כמוהו רדב"ז ח"א סי' נ"ט וכה"ג. ועיין שו"ת שער אפרים סי' כ"ו. תוקע שמת ונכנס אחר במקומו וכשגדל בנו רוצה לירש זכות אביו ע' הלק"ט סי' ל"ט. וע' בספר קול בן לוי דף כ"ח ע"ג:
baer_heitev.en: On the way. The Yerushalmi: this was stated only regarding one who is passing by; but regarding one who is standing, there is a chazakah that he intended. And this requires further study: is he not one who knows whether he intended or not? And perhaps it refers to where he forgot whether he intended or not (Magen Avraham. One who comes to the synagogue to fulfill his obligation with the congregation) even though at the time he heard he did not direct his heart, but only in a general way; has fulfilled; but one who comes to the synagogue in a general way has not fulfilled (Radbaz, part 1, siman 160). A blind person is obligated in tekiah; and if he was established to blow every year and they removed him, if they do not find one as expert as he, they should restore him to his appointment. And l'chatchila one should not remove him because he is blind, even though another as expert as he is found (Radbaz, part 1, siman 59; and Kenesses HaGedolah). And see Responsa Shaar Ephraim, siman 26. A blower who died and another entered in his place, and when his son grew up he wished to inherit his father's right (see Halachot Ketanot, siman 39). And see the Sefer Kol Ben Levi, folio 28c.

beur_hagra.he: ס"ט מהלך. ירושלמי ל"ש אלא בעובר אבל בעומד חזקה כיון והביאו הר"ן וז"ש מהלך בדרך או כו':
beur_hagra.en: Seif 9: One who is walking. The Jerusalem Talmud states that this applies only to one who is passing by. If he stands still, it is presumed that he intended to fulfill the mitzvah. Ran cites this. This is the meaning of the words, “walking on the road, or,” etc.

chokhmat_shlomo.he: (שם סעיף ט') לפיכך מי שהיה מהלך בדרך או יושב בתוך ביתו ושמע תקיעות משליח ציבור יצא וכו'. נ"ב עיין במג"א שהביא מ"ש הר"ן בשם הירושלמי וז"ל בד"א בעובר אבל בעומד חזקה כיוון עכ"ל והמג"א תמה דהרי הוא ידע אם כוון או לא ע"ש שנדחק בזה. ולפענ"ר נראה דנ"מ טובא לפי מה דאיתא לעיל בש"ע. סי' ר"ט ס"ח בהג"ה שאם היו אחרים שותין יין וכו' ובירך בפה"ג שסבר דבכוסו הוי יין ונודע לו שהיה מים כשרוצה לשתות אחר כך יין א"צ לברך כיון דדעתו הוי לשתות יין אח"כ גם הוציא אחרים בברכתו לכך הוי ברכתו ברכה ע"ש ואם כן ה"נ כיון דקיי"ל שמע ט' תקיעות בט' שעות ביום יצא ואם כן נ"מ אם המהלך היה צריך לתרועה דתקיעה כבר שמע עדיין לא שמע גם הקיעה והי' חייב תקיעה תחלה ובירך על השופר והתחיל לתקוע תרועה תחלה וכיון דתרועה קודם לתקיעה לא יצא ממילא הוי הפסק בין ברכה לתחלת התקיעה וצריך לחזור ולברך אך בזה כיון דהשומע היה צריך לתרועה אם כן אותו היוצא בברכה זו ותקיעה זו לכך כיון דאת אחרים הוציא גם דעתו היה לתקוע עוד אין זה ברכה לבטלה ומותר לתקוע אח"כ בסדר על סמך ברכה ראשונה ואם כן תינח אם כוון השומע לצאת אבל לא כוון אם כן לא הוציא אחרים ושוב הוי ברכתו לבטלה וצריך לברך מחדש וא"כ כיון דבאתחזיק חיובא או איסורא אין ע"א נאמן להיפוך דהוי נגד החזקה ולכך אם לא הוי חזקה דכוון רק שהוא היה אומר שכוון לא היה נאמן הוא לפטור את התוקע מברכה שנית כיון דנתחייב לברך אין ע"א נאמן לפוטרו אבל אם אמרינן דחזקה כוון אם כן הוציא אחרים בברכתו לכך גם הוא פטור מלברך. ועוד נראה יותר כיון דדין זה גופא שכתב הרמ"א בסי' ר"ט חידוש הוא דלומד כיון דהם יצאו גם הוא יוצא והסברא נותנת להיפוך כיון דהוא בירך לבטלה גם הם לא יצאו ויותר יש לתלות אחרים בו מלתלות אותו באחרים וכמ"ש המג"א שם ועיין סי' רי"ג ס"ב שהקשה המג"א דברי הש"ע אהדדי ותירץ לחלק בין שוגג למזיד והוא דוחק דמה סברא יש לחלק בין שוגג למזיד ואין לו' דבמזיד הוי מטעם קנס חדא דלא מצינו דמשום קנס יחזרו לברך ברכה אחרת לבטלה ועוד אף אם קנסוהו הרי אחרים לא חטאו ולמה לנו לקנוס אותם ומה סברא לחלק לענין אחרים בין אם הוי המברך שוגג או מזיד. אך נראה דלא לחנם דייק הרמ"א בסי' ר"ט שכתב דהיו אחרים שותין יין ויין לפניהם דלמה לו לו' שהיה יין לפניהם. אך נראה ניהו דבעלמא לא בעינן אומדנא דמוכח וגילוי דעת שהשומע מכוין לצאת רק די בכוונה בלב שמכוונים לצאת מ"מ זה הוי דוקא אם המברך יצא אז כיון דהברכה שלו הוי כדין והוא יצא אז לא מהני במחשבתן לבד דק אם הוי במחשבתן ניכר מתוך מעשיהם אז כיון דמוכח בש"ס בכמה דוכתא דמחשבתו הניכר מתוך מעשיו עדיף ממחשבה גרידא והוי כמעשה עיין בפ"ב דביצה ובפ"ק דחולין ולכך אם יש יין לפניהם דהוי מחשבתם ניכר מתוך מעשיהם דרוצין לצאת הוי כאלו ברכו הם ממש בעצמם ואם כן מה בכך דהוא בירך לבטלה הם יוצאים דהוי כאלו ברכו הם ממש דבזה הוי כמעשה ממש אבל אם אין מחשבתן ניכר מתוך מעשיהם רק בכוונת הלב בלבד בזה לא הוי כברכו הם ממש רק ששמעו ובשמיעה אין די כיון דהוא בירך לבטלה ולכך בסי' רי"ג מיירי דלא הוי אומדנא דמוכח ממעשיהם רק שאמרו שכוונו לכך לא מהני כיון דבירך הוא לבטלה אבל אם יש אומדנא דמוכח ממעשיהם מהני וזה כמו הדין דסי' ר"ט הנ"ל ואם כן לפי"ז א"ש הירושלמי על נכון דנ"מ אם בירך התוקע והריע תחלה קודם התקיעה דהוי הפסק בין הברכה לתחלת התקיעה והוי לבטלה אז עמד השומע דחזקה דכוון ויצא השומע אף שהמברך בירך לבטלה ואז אדרבא גם המברך יצא כמ"ש בסי' ר"ט וז"ב ונכון בסברא מאד. ואם נימא כמ"ש תחלה דבזה אין השומע נאמן נגד השני כיון דאתחזיק חיובא י"ל עוד נ"מ לפמ"ש בסי' תקפ"ה דאם בירך ולא יכול לתקוע יתקעו אחרים בלא ברכה והוא שיהיו תוקעים הראשונים בשעת ברכה משמע דתרוייהו בעינן שיהיו השומעים בשעת ברכה וגם התוקעים היו אז אבל אם לא היו שם התוקעים אף שהיו שם השומעים לא מהני ואם כן נ"מ אם לא היה תוקע רק זה שעמד בדרך אז אם עמד כיון דהוי הזקה שכוון מותר לתקוע אחר כך בלא ברכה ופוטר את השומעים אבל אם הלך כיון דהוי ספק אם כוון אינו נאמן לו' שכוון לפטור את השומעים מהברכה כיון דנתחייבו בו בוודאי אין ע"א נאמן לפטור דאין ע"א נאמן נגד החזקה כך הוי נראה לו'. מיהו באמת אינו נראה כן דאף לולא עדותו כיון דעכ"פ ספק הוי הרי קיי"ל ספק ברכות להקל ולא מצינו לחלק בין אם הוי ספק בעיקר החיוב בין אם נתחייב בודאי וספק אם נפטר רק בכל ענין הוי ספק ברכות להקל וא"כ בלאו עדותו פטור מספק. לכך נראה דהעיקר כתירוץ אמצעי שכתבנו דבזה בעינן מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו ובלא"ה בודאי הוי ברכה לבטלה בלי ספק כלל ואתי שפיר ונכון בעזה"י ודו"ק היטב:
chokhmat_shlomo.en: (There, se'if 9) Therefore one who was walking on the way or sitting in his house and heard tekios from the agent of the congregation has fulfilled, etc. Gloss: See the Magen Avraham, who brought what the Ran wrote in the name of the Yerushalmi, and this is his language: "When is this said? Regarding one who is passing by; but regarding one who is standing, there is a chazakah that he intended" (end quote. And the Magen Avraham wondered: for does he not know whether he intended or not?) see there, where he was pressed on this. And in my humble opinion it appears that there is a great practical difference according to what is stated above in the Shulchan Aruch, siman 209, se'if 8 in the gloss: that if others were drinking wine, etc., and he recited the blessing "Who creates the fruit of the vine," thinking that in his cup there was wine, and it became known to him that it was water, when he afterward wishes to drink wine he need not recite the blessing, since his intent was to drink wine afterward, and he also discharged others with his blessing; therefore his blessing was a blessing (see there. And so here too: since we hold that one who heard nine tekios at nine hours of the day has fulfilled) and so there is a difference: if the one walking needed a teruah, for he had already heard a tekiah but had not yet heard also a tekiah, and he was obligated in a tekiah first, and he recited the blessing over the shofar and began to blow a teruah first, and since a teruah before a tekiah [means] he has not fulfilled, automatically there was an interruption between the blessing and the beginning of the tekiah, and he must recite the blessing again. But in this case, since the hearer needed a teruah, and so that one [who recited] discharged [others] with this blessing and this tekiah; therefore, since he discharged others, and his intent was also to blow further, this is not a blessing in vain, and he is permitted to blow afterward in order on the strength of the first blessing. And so this is fine if the hearer intended to fulfill; but if he did not intend, then he did not discharge others, and again his blessing was in vain, and he must recite the blessing anew. And so, since where an obligation or prohibition has been established, one witness is not believed to the contrary, for it is against the chazakah, therefore if there were no chazakah that he intended, but only that he said he intended, he would not be believed to exempt the blower from a second blessing, since having become obligated to recite the blessing, one witness is not believed to exempt him; but if we say there is a chazakah that he intended, then he discharged others with his blessing, and therefore he too is exempt from blessing. And it appears further: since this very law that the Rama wrote in siman 209 is a novelty (that he learns that since they fulfilled, he too fulfills) and reason would suggest the opposite: since he recited a blessing in vain, they too have not fulfilled; and it is more [natural] to subordinate others to him than to subordinate him to others, as the Magen Avraham wrote there. And see siman 213, se'if 2, where the Magen Avraham raised a difficulty that the Shulchan Aruch's words contradict one another, and answered by distinguishing between inadvertent and intentional, and it is forced: what reason is there to distinguish between inadvertent and intentional? And one cannot say that for the intentional it is by way of a fine; first, we do not find that because of a fine they should again recite another blessing in vain; and further, even if they fined him, others did not sin; why should we fine them? And what reason is there to distinguish regarding others between whether the one who blessed was inadvertent or intentional? But it appears that not for nothing did the Rama specify in siman 209 that he wrote that others were drinking wine and wine was before them; why tell us that wine was before them? But it appears: although in general we do not require a proven presumption and revelation of intent that the hearer intends to fulfill (mere intent in the heart that they intend to fulfill suffices) nevertheless this is specifically if the one who blessed fulfilled; then, since his blessing was according to law and he fulfilled, then [for them] mere thought alone does not help unless their thought is recognizable from their deeds; then, since it is evident in the Gemara in several places that thought recognizable from one's deeds is superior to mere thought and is like an act (see in chapter 2 of Beitzah and in the first chapter of Chullin) therefore if there is wine before them, so that their thought is recognizable from their deeds that they wish to fulfill, it is as if they themselves recited the blessing; and so what of it that he recited a blessing in vain; they fulfill, for it is as if they themselves recited, for in this it is like an actual act. But if their thought is not recognizable from their deeds, but only by intent of the heart alone, in that case it is not as if they themselves recited, but only that they heard; and hearing does not suffice, since he recited a blessing in vain. And therefore in siman 213 it refers to where there was no proven presumption from their deeds, but only that they said they intended (therefore it does not help, since he recited a blessing in vain; but if there is a proven presumption from their deeds, it helps) and this is like the law of siman 209 above. And so according to this the Yerushalmi is well resolved: the practical difference is if the blower recited the blessing and sounded a teruah first before the tekiah, so that there was an interruption between the blessing and the beginning of the tekiah and it was in vain, then if the hearer stood, there is a chazakah that he intended, and the hearer fulfilled even though the one who blessed recited in vain; and then on the contrary the one who blessed also fulfilled, as is written in siman 209; and this is clear and very correct in reason. And if we say as I wrote at first (that in this the hearer is not believed against the other, since an obligation was established) one may say further a practical difference according to what is written in siman 585: that if he recited the blessing and could not blow, others should blow without a blessing (provided that the first blowers were [present] at the time of the blessing; implying that we require both) that the hearers be present at the time of the blessing and also that the blowers were then [present]; but if the blowers were not there, even though the hearers were there, it does not help. And so there is a difference: if there was no blower other than this one who stood on the way, then if he stood, since there is a chazakah that he intended, it is permitted afterward to blow without a blessing and he discharges the hearers; but if he walked, since it is a doubt whether he intended, he is not believed to say that he intended so as to exempt the hearers from the blessing (since they became obligated with certainty, one witness is not believed to exempt, for one witness is not believed against a chazakah) so it would appear to say. However, in truth this does not appear correct: for even without his testimony, since at any rate it is a doubt, behold we hold that a doubt regarding blessings is resolved leniently; and we do not find a distinction between whether the doubt is in the root of the obligation or whether he became obligated with certainty and there is a doubt whether he was exempted; rather in every case a doubt regarding blessings is resolved leniently; and so even without his testimony he is exempt out of doubt. Therefore it appears that the main [resolution] is the middle answer we wrote: that in this we require that his thought be recognizable from his deeds; and otherwise it is certainly a blessing in vain without any doubt; and it fits well and is correct, with the help of Hashem; and examine carefully.

eliyah_rabbah.he: [ט] [לבוש] העובר לפני בית הכנסת וכו'. אבל עומד חזקה כיוון (ירושלמי). ונראה לי דוקא כשעובר ועמד, אבל בהיה עומד בתוך ביתו לא הוי חזקה. מי שבא לבית הכנסת לצאת ידי חובתו עם הציבור אף שבשעה ששמע לא כיוון לבו אלא סתמא יצא, אבל הבא לבית הכנסת בסתמא לא יצא, רדב"ז כנסת הגדולה מגן אברהם. ולענין ריחוק מבית הכנסת אם נראה לו ברור שקול שופר שמע יצא, ט"ז סימן תקפ"ז:
eliyah_rabbah.en: [9] [Levush] One who passes before the synagogue, etc. But one who is standing; there is a chazakah that he intended (Yerushalmi). And it appears to me that this is specifically when he was passing and [then] stood; but if he was standing inside his house, there is no such chazakah. One who comes to the synagogue to fulfill his obligation with the congregation (even though at the time he heard he did not direct his heart, but only in a general way) has fulfilled; but one who comes to the synagogue in a general way has not fulfilled (Radbaz; Kenesses HaGedolah; Magen Avraham). And regarding distance from the synagogue: if it is clear to him that he heard a shofar sound, he has fulfilled (Taz, siman 587).

magen_avraham.he: מהלך בדרך כו'. ירושלמי ל"ש אלא בעובר אבל בעומד חזק' כוון (ר"ן) וצ"ע הלא הוא יודע אם כוון אם לאו ואפשר דמיירי אם שכח אם כוון אם לא:
magen_avraham.en: walking on the road etc. Yerushalmi L.S. except in the past, but in a strong position, he aimed (Ra'n) and TSA otherwise he knows whether he aimed or not and it is possible to imagine if he forgot if he aimed or not:

mishnah_berurah.he:
(יז) שישמענו - אבל אם היו תוקעין בבית לחולה וליולדת והיה ביתו סמוך לו ושמע לא יצא דמסתמא לא נתכוין זה להוציא אלא החולה [ח"א]:
(יח) מי שהיה מהלך בדרך וכו' אם נתכוון לצאת וכו' - איתא בירושלמי לא שנו אלא בעובר אבל בעומד חזקה כיון ועיין בא"ר שכתב דכונת הירושלמי בעובר ועומד לשמוע קול תקיעות דאז אמרינן אף דאינו זוכר אם כיון אז לצאת מ"מ חזקה שכיון אבל בשהיה עומד בביתו לא אמרינן חזקה כיון. סומא חייב בתקיעות ואם היה מוחזק לתקוע בכל שנה וסלקוהו אם לא ימצאו בקי כמוהו יחזירוהו למנויו. ולכתחלה אין לסלקו מפני שהוא סומא אע"פ שנמצא בקי כמוהו [מ"א בשם הרדב"ז]:
(יט) ושמע תקיעות משליח צבור וכו' - ובלבד שלא עמד רחוק מביהכ"נ כ"כ שאפשר שלא ישמע קול שופר רק קול הברה:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(17) That he hear him; but if they were blowing in a house for a sick person or a woman who has given birth, and his house was adjacent to it and he heard, he has not fulfilled; for presumably he intended to discharge only the sick person [Chayei Adam].
(18) One who was walking on the way, etc., if he intended to fulfill, etc. It is stated in the Yerushalmi: this was taught only regarding one who is passing by; but regarding one who is standing, there is a chazakah that he intended. And see the Eliyah Rabbah, who wrote that the Yerushalmi's intent is regarding one who was passing and stood to hear the sound of the tekios, for then we say that even if he does not remember whether he then intended to fulfill, nevertheless there is a chazakah that he intended; but if he was standing in his house, we do not say there is a chazakah that he intended. A blind person is obligated in the tekios; and if he was established to blow every year and they removed him, if they do not find one as expert as he, they should restore him to his appointment. And l'chatchila one should not remove him because he is blind, even though another as expert as he is found [Magen Avraham in the name of the Radbaz].
(19) And he heard tekios from the agent of the congregation, etc., provided he did not stand so far from the synagogue that it is possible he heard not a shofar sound but only an echo.

shaarei_teshuvah.he: בדרך, עבה"ט וכ' בשמש צדקה סי' ך"ט שהקשו לו על מ"ש ה"ה פ"ב מהל' שופר דלכך צריך כוונה כיון דעיקר המצוה הוא השמיעה ואפי' התוקע משא"כ באכילת מצה כולי דקשה ע"ז מדין חליצה דהוי מעשה וע"ש שכתב ליישב זה באורך ובתשובת בן המחבר מברר ענין צריכים הכוונ' במצות ע"ש וה"ש הרדב"ז בענין סומא ע' בדבר שמואל סי' י"ב הסומא מוציא אחרים בתקיעת שופר ובכל מצות דאורייתא ע"ש:
shaarei_teshuvah.en: On the way. See Baer Heitev; and he wrote in Shemesh Tzedakah, siman 29, that they raised a difficulty against what the Maggid Mishneh wrote in chapter 2 of Hilchos Shofar; that therefore intent is required, since the essence of the mitzvah is the hearing, and even the blower [needs intent], which is not so regarding eating matzah, etc., for it is difficult against this from the law of chalitzah, which is an act; and see there, where he wrote at length to resolve this. And in the responsum of the author's son he clarifies the matter of whether mitzvos require intent (see there. And that which the Radbaz wrote regarding a blind person) see Devar Shmuel, siman 12: a blind person discharges others with shofar-blowing and with all Torah mitzvos (see there).

kaf_hachayyim.he: ט) ביום א' דר"ה התוקע לא עצר כח בתקיעה שעל סדר הברכות ותקע קטן שהגיע לי"ג שנים ולא ידעו אם הביא סימנים יוצאים בו כיון דתקיעה דאו' כבר יצאו בתקיעות דמיושב ובדרבנן סמכינן אחזקה שהביא ב' שערות. תשו' שואל ומשיב ח"ג סי' קע"ז יעו"ש. פ"ת פת"ע או' ב' ועיין לעיל סי' נ"ה סעי' ה' בהגה ובדברינו לשם בס"ד:
kaf_hachayyim.en: 9) On the first day of Rosh Hashanah, if the shofar blower lacked the strength to sound the blasts arranged during the blessings, and a minor who had reached 13 years sounded them, but it was not known whether he had developed the signs of maturity, the congregation fulfills its obligation through him. This is because they had already fulfilled the Torah obligation through the blasts sounded while seated, and for a rabbinic obligation we rely on the presumption that he developed two pubic hairs. Responsa Shoel U'Meishiv, vol. 3, siman 177, see there; Pitchei Teshuvah; Pischei Olam, os 2. See above, siman 55, seif 5, in the Rama's gloss, and our words there, with God's help.
